title: Hierarchically Porous COFs Enabled by Copolymer‐Mediated Mechanochemical Preassembly
abstract: ABSTRACT The relatively small pore channels of conventional covalent organic frameworks (COFs) would impede mass transport and limit the accessibility of active sites therein, restricting their practical utility with bulky molecules. Here, we break this bottleneck by developing a copolymer‐mediated mechanochemistry strategy that enables the construction of hierarchically porous COF (HPCOF) precursors with tunable large mesopores, which are then recrystallized to afford crystalline HPCOFs. The confined microenvironments of low‐solvent ball‐milling not only enhance hydrogen‐bonding interactions between monomers and Pluronic F127 (PEO 106 PPO 70 PEO 106 ) micelles, but also eliminate the disruptive effects of excess solvent and acidic conditions on micelle assembly. Additionally, the mechanical pulses decompose the polycondensation into stepwise events, effectively buffering the incompatible rates between the polymerization of COF precursors and micelle assembly and allowing the mesostructures to be precisely “locked” under solid‐state confined conditions. By varying monomer combinations, seven representative HPCOFs with different connectivities were constructed. Thanks to its simplicity and reproducibility, the proposed strategy demonstrates potential in large‐scale production. Benefiting from the synergistic combination of large channels and rigid microporous crystalline walls, the resultant HPCOFs feature unique structural stability and favorable enzyme affinity, enabling efficient trypsin immobilization with retained catalytic activity for protein hydrolysis, prefiguring their application prospects in bioreactor construction.

title: Cofactor‐Inspired Second‐Sphere Engineering of Artificial Metalloenzymes for Neutral Ammonia Synthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Constructing artificial metalloenzymes with precisely positioned metal centers and tailored second‐sphere microenvironments remains challenging in replicating the hierarchical catalytic functions of natural enzymes. Here, we report a cofactor‐inspired second‐sphere engineering strategy to construct an artificial nanozyme, CuS 1 /CN, featuring atomically defined [3Cu−1S] motifs selectively anchored to ultrasmall Cu clusters (∼0.73 nm) within a mesoporous nitrogen‐doped carbon framework. This architecture establishes enzyme‐like catalytic compartmentalization without compromising active‐site accessibility: exposed Cu sites mimic nitrate reductase for nitrate activation and water dissociation, while adjacent [3Cu−1S] motifs function as cofactor‐like centers that orchestrate interfacial hydration, facilitating proton‐coupled electron transfer and hydrogen relay during downstream hydrogenation. The engineered second‐sphere microenvironment overcomes the intrinsic *NO 2 ‐to‐*NO 2 H bottleneck and shifts the rate‐determining step to *NH 2 O‐to‐*NH 2 OH conversion with a substantially reduced energy barrier. Consequently, CuS 1 /CN enables highly efficient and selective ammonia electrosynthesis under neutral conditions at industrially relevant current densities with long‐term stability. Its integration into a Zn−NO 3 − battery further enables simultaneous nitrate conversion and electricity generation. This work establishes cofactor‐inspired second‐sphere engineering as a general strategy for designing artificial enzymes with programmable catalytic microenvironments beyond conventional active‐site engineering.

title: Macrocycle 2D COF Single Crystal
abstract: Abstract We report the synthesis of a two-dimensional (2D) covalent organic framework (COF) single crystal, termed COF-900, constructed from a geminiarene-type macrocycle linker, biphenyl-extended pillar[3]arene containing nine phenyl units. The atomically accurate structure was resolved by three-dimensional electron diffraction (3D ED) of the 2D COF single crystal with a resolution of 1.2 Å, unveiling the conformation of the macrocycle in the layered backbone as well as AB interlayer stacking. The macrocycle exhibits a similar stacking mode in both the COF and the molecular crystal of the linker, suggesting prealignment of linkers during COF crystal growth through a mechanism termed alignment-led framework assembly (ALFA). Cryo-transmission electron microscopy images further provided direct real-space visualization of the macrocycle, where three types of interconnected pores were clearly visualized with sizes of 1.1, 1.5, and 2.3 nm.

title: Orthogonal Self‐Assembled Two‐Dimensional Charge‐Transfer Cocrystals With Superior Photothermal Stability for Low‐Loss NIR‐II Waveguiding and Epitaxial Heterostructure Fabrication
abstract: ABSTRACT Low‐dimensional organic near‐infrared (NIR) crystals hold tremendous potential for integrated photonics. However, simultaneously achieving two‐dimensional (2D) structural growth and low‐loss waveguiding within the NIR‐II region remains a formidable challenge due to one‐dimensional (1D) packing tendencies imposed by strong charge transfer (CT) interactions. In this study, we strategically choose the extended π‐conjugated structure donor dithieno[2,3‐d:2',3'‐d']benzo[1,2‐b:4,5‐b']dithiophene and the strong electron‐withdrawing acceptor tetracyanoquinodimethane, and report the first large‐scale preparation of 2D organic CT cocrystal microsheets with NIR‐II emission at 1050 nm via a gas‐phase self‐assembly. The strategically expanded conjugation framework not only further promotes the luminescence red‐shift but also introduces an interaction network with orthogonal directions, counterbalancing the intrinsic 1D stacking constraints brought by the strong CT interactions and guiding the crystals into a thermodynamically stable 2D morphology. The compact network plays a crucial role in endowing the material with exceptional structural and photothermal stability, as well as low‐loss optical waveguiding. Furthermore, attributed to the extremely low lattice‐mismatch rate, 1D‐2D branched heterostructures were constructed, which demonstrated efficient energy transfer (ET) and cross‐band optical signal conversion over 600 nm. This work breaks new ground in extending 2D organic cocrystals into the NIR‐II region and provides a promising material platform for low‐loss, and integrated NIR optoelectronic devices.

title: An Interfacial Electron Pump Enhanced Photo‐Assisted CO 2 ‐to‐Bioplastic Microbial Electrosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Most solar‐ and electrochemical CO 2 ‐utilization strategies still terminate in small‐molecule products, whereas direct access to recoverable carbon products such as bioplastics remains uncommon. Here, we develop a photo‐assisted bioelectrochemical platform by coupling a Shewanella oneidensis MR‐1 bioanode functionalized with Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene quantum dots (MQDs) to a Cupriavidus necator biocathode modified with Ni‐doped carbon dots/poly(diallyldimethylammonium chloride) (Ni‐CDs/PDDA). Cell‐associated MQDs form a conductive and photoactive biointerface, operationally described as an interfacial electron pump, that facilitates lactate‐dependent extracellular electron transfer (EET) under applied anodic bias and adds an illumination‐dependent current contribution. The MQDs‐enabled microbial fuel cell (MFC) delivers a peak power density of 0.82 ± 0.03 mW cm −2 under illumination. In the coupled CO 2 ‐fed system, anodic illumination raises polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB) productivity to 131 mg L −1 d −1 at −0.6 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode (vs. RHE), approximately 47% above the matched dark value over a 12 h interval. The coupled platform reaches an apparent total‐energy‐to‐PHB efficiency of 3.42% when electrical, incident optical, and lactate‐derived chemical inputs are included. Multiscale analyses support an EET‐coupled interfacial relay involving cytochrome/heme‐associated components within the native EET network. This interface‐to‐synthesis strategy links photo‐assisted microbial electron harvesting to H 2 ‐mediated CO 2 ‐to‐PHB biosynthesis.

title: Flexible 2D Donor‐Acceptor MOFs Enable Tunable and Pressure‐Responsive TSCT–TADF for Heterocrystal Photonic Logic
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) materials that combine high efficiency, color tunability, and dynamic stimulus responsiveness are highly desirable for adaptive photonic technologies, yet remain difficult to realize within a single crystalline platform. Here, flexible two‐dimensional (2D) donor‐acceptor (D–A) metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) are developed through integrating an aggregation‐induced‐emission‐active triphenylamine donor with size‐matched electron‐deficient acceptors. Solvent‐directed assembly, donor conformational flexibility, and acceptor electronic modulation cooperatively regulate the D–A packing and through‐space charge‐transfer (TSCT) effect. The resulting MOFs exhibit broadly tunable TADF emission (474–635 nm), delayed lifetimes (0.11–7.65 µs), and photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQY, 0.52%–74.24%). Relative to the DMF‐derived structures, the DMA‐derived MOFs display increases of up to 51‐fold in delayed lifetime and 6‐fold in PLQY, while calculations support an unconventional high‐lying reverse intersystem crossing (hRISC) pathway. More importantly, the structural adaptability of the layered frameworks enables pressure‐induced reconfiguration of D–A interactions, giving rise to reversible piezochromic TSCT–TADF with emission shifts of up to 113 nm. A multicomponent heterocrystal is further constructed to translate pressure‐dependent emission changes into optical logic operations. These results establish flexible 2D D–A MOFs as a dynamic platform for integrating efficient TADF, mechanical responsiveness, and heterocrystal photonic functionality.

title: Guest-Mediated On-Surface Growth of 2D COF Heterobilayer for Synaptic Devices
abstract: Abstract Chemically defined organic heterobilayers offer a route to programmable interfacial coupling, yet their on-surface construction remains challenging due to the instability of dynamic covalent frameworks during sequential growth. Here, we report a guest-induced COF-on-COF growth strategy that enables deterministic heteroepitaxy of imine/boroxine covalent organic framework (COF) heterobilayers at solid–liquid interfaces. Coronene guest molecules occupy the pores of the underlying imine COF, stabilizing the framework while promoting interfacial molecular diffusion, thereby redirecting growth from framework degradation to directional epitaxy. This yields a structurally precise heterobilayer with a commensurate √3 × √3 R30° rotational relationship and long-range order. The resulting 2D COF heterobilayer is continuous over large areas with low defect density, enabling direct device integration without transfer. Electrical measurements, supported by theory, reveal interfacial charge redistribution arising from chemically encoded asymmetry, manifested as interfacial charge redistribution and enhanced charge trapping. Device responses, including nonvolatile switching and analogue conductance modulation, provide a macroscopic readout of the molecularly defined heterointerface. These results establish a route to programmable organic heterostructures in which interfacial growth, coupling, and electronic functionality are codesigned through molecular assembly.

title: Synthetic Pathway Modulation of Metal Organization in Multivariate Metal–Organic Frameworks
abstract: ABSTRACT Multivariate metal–organic frameworks (MTV MOFs) incorporate various metals and/or linkers within a periodic backbone, offering structural diversity and emergent functionalities. Typically, conventional one‐pot synthesis does not allow for any control over the spatial arrangement or sequencing of metals within the framework. Here, we present a synthetic strategy to alter metal arrangement in multimetallic MTV MOFs, yielding materials with nearly identical composition yet distinct properties. Using isostructural m CB‐Co and m CB‐Ni MOFs, we generate two MTV MOFs with different one‐dimensional Ni/Co arrangements, resulting in distinct semiconducting and magnetic properties. High‐resolution electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (ESI‐HRMS) reveals the formation of distinct precursor species in solution, suggesting that prenucleation chemistry influences the final metal arrangement. This work establishes a new approach for modulating metal arrangement in MTV MOFs, enabling tunable functional properties in multimetallic frameworks for applications in catalysis, electronics, and quantum materials.

title: Solar-Matched Colloidal Quantum Dots/Metal–Organic Framework Hybrid Materials for Photo-Induced Charge Transfer
abstract: Abstract Lead sulfide colloidal quantum dots (PbS CQDs) are promising third-generation photovoltaic materials, and metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are complementary materials that are used as multifunctional charge storage and redox platforms. Hybrid materials combining CQDs and MOFs are highly promising for applications utilizing solar-driven charge transfer, but their synthesis can be challenging due to the thermal instability of solar-matched infrared CQDs. Here, we demonstrate a room-temperature, "bottle-around-ship" synthesis of a nanocomposite that integrates near-infrared (NIR) absorbing PbS CQDs with an iron-based MOF, MIL-88B(Fe). We employ a syringe-pump-assisted addition of precursors to achieve controlled nucleation and crystallization of the MOF around the CQDs under ambient conditions. Structural characterization confirms the formation of crystalline composites composed of co-localized CQDs with the MOFs. Steady-state, time-resolved optical spectroscopy reveals photoluminescence quenching and shortening of the exciton lifetime in the composite compared to the CQDs alone. Transient absorption data suggest a photo-induced charge transfer from the PbS CQDs to the MIL-88B(Fe) framework on a picosecond timescale. This work establishes a room-temperature synthesis approach for integrating thermally sensitive solar-matched CQDs with functional MOFs and performs an initial spectroscopic study to evaluate the potential of these nanocomposites as advanced hybrid materials for photocatalysis and optoelectrochemical devices in the future.

title: Ultrarobust and Thermo‐Mechano‐Photo‐Responsive Elastomers by Supramolecular and Dynamic 3D Topological Architectures
abstract: ABSTRACT Mechanically robust elastomers are being widely used in multi‐stimuli‐responsive systems including closed‐loop recycling, information encryption, and advanced photolithography. However, their advancement is hindered by an inherent trade‐off: structural integrity for mechanical robustness versus molecular‐level reversibility for stimuli responsiveness. In this study, we constructed ultrarobust recyclable and photo‐responsive supramolecular‐dynamic covalent networks (SDCN) based on molecular engineering of anthracene‐functionalized poly(urethane‐urea‐amide) (PUUA) networks with hindered urea motifs. Well‐designed SDCN achieves multiscale assembly through coordinated π–π stacking, hydrogen bonding, and dynamic covalent interactions, creating dynamic coupling between soft‐chain crosslinks and self‐assembly hard domains, and driving microphase separation. Under stretching, strain‐activated disassembly of dynamically assembled nanostructures synergizes with stress‐induced crystallization, in situ evolving three‐dimensional topological architectures and promoting strength‐toughness enhancement. Consequently, PUUA elastomers exhibit remarkable mechanical performance (100.17 MPa tensile strength, 1286.79% elongation and 498.15 MJ m −3 toughness at room temperature; 113.67 MPa strength and 667.8% elongation at −40°C) and recycling performance (92.4% recyclability via solvent reprocessing). Significantly, UV‐responsive anthracene photonic moieties combined with temperature‐mediated interfacial SDCN transition enable fluorescent encryption and sub‐micron photolithographic patterning. Therefore, this work coordinates dynamic thermal‐mechanical‐optical responses and multi‐scale molecular transition mechanisms, which can be expected to boost high‐precision photolithographic patterning and flexible microcircuit printing fields.

title: Deferoxamine‐Engineered Mesoporous Silica Nanoparticles Unlock High‐Valence Metal Channels for Multiplexed Mass Cytometry
abstract: ABSTRACT Mass cytometry (MC) enables highly multiplexed single‐cell protein analysis, but its full analytical potential remains constrained by the limited range of available mass tags. Here, we report deferoxamine‐engineered mesoporous silica nanoparticles (DFO‐MSNs) for high‐capacity loading of multiple underutilized high‐valent metal ions within a common nanoparticle scaffold. DFO‐MSNs accommodated Zr 4+ , Hf 4+ , Nb 5+ , and Ta 5+ at approximately 10 4 metal atoms per nanoparticle, with high metal retention in physiological buffers. Following PEGylation and antibody (Ab) conjugation, the resulting Zr‐, Nb‐, Hf‐, and Ta‐based probes enabled antigen‐specific detection of human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) by co‐staining with commercial Maxpar reagents. Nb‐, Hf‐, and Ta‐loaded MSN_CD8a probes resolved CD8a+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes at titers as low as 30 NPs/cell. In a 30‐plex staining panel, Ta@MSN_CD25 resolved low‐abundance CD25 hi CD127 lo T reg ‐like cells with apparent population recovery comparable to the corresponding Maxpar reagent, while consuming ca. 35‐fold less Ab. Together, these results establish a modular strategy for incorporating underutilized high‐valent metals into functional mass tags and demonstrate the feasibility of integrating MSN‐based probes into multiplexed MC immunophenotyping workflows.

title: Zeolite Crystallization via Seed-Mediated Chemical Vapor Deposition
abstract: Abstract The demand for zeolites with specific, tailored characteristics is expected to further accelerate. For decades, however, zeolites have been predominantly synthesized by hydrothermal methods, in which tightly coupled sol–gel processes, nucleation, and crystal growth constrain property control and complicate device-oriented fabrication. Here we report the direct synthesis of zeolites by chemical vapor deposition (CVD), in which vapor-delivered precursors crystallize on preexisting zeolite seeds. Mechanistic investigations reveal that zeolite growth under CVD follows a fundamentally distinct pathway, where vapor-phase hydrolysis–condensation reactions are spatially decoupled from interfacial crystallization. This decoupling enables the maintenance of a controlled and steady supersaturation, offering a facile strategy for fabricating zeolite films with low dielectric constants and robust mechanical properties. The unique mechanism and operation mode of CVD bring zeolite crystallization into a manufacturing-relevant vapor-phase regime that could be extended to other zeolite types and deployed in diverse applications.

title: When Electrolytes Become Dopants: Programming Charge Transport in Conductive Metal−Organic Framework Transistors
abstract: Abstract Conjugated metal−organic frameworks (c-MOFs) operating in ionic environments have emerged as promising microporous and conductive systems for next-generation applications. Understanding the interplay between electrolyte composition and electronic−ionic mixed transport remains a critical barrier to the rational design of novel devices. Here, we demonstrate that electrolyte composition provides a direct and programmable handle for controlling charge transport and field-effect properties in c-MOF electrochemical transistors (ECTs). Two types of c-MOF thin films composed of the conjugated linker 2,3,5,6,10,11-hexahydroxytriphenylene (HHTP) and either Cu2+ or Ni2+ ions, namely, Cu3(HHTP)2 and Ni3(HHTP)2, were employed as transistor channel materials. Using these c-MOFs as prototypical conductive frameworks, we systematically interrogate the influence of ionic strength, ion identity, pH, and gate configuration on transistor operation. Across these variables, we unveil robust and quantitative relationships linking the nature and conditions of the electrolyte to variations in charge neutrality, modulation of transconductance, and transitions between transport regimes. For instance, increasing ionic strength shifts the transfer curves of Cu3(HHTP)2- and Ni3(HHTP)2-based ECTs toward a more negative potential, with a linear dependence on the logarithm of ion concentration. The ion-hydrated radius strongly influences ion-electron transport, as smaller cations more readily permeate the framework and reduce surface potential. Charge neutrality point potential (VCNP) displays a linear pH dependence, with sensitivities comparable to conducting polymer ECTs. Device performance is also influenced by the gate electrode configuration (liquid-junction or pseudo-reference electrodes). Extensive field-effect characterization demonstrates good electrochemical stability. A unified mechanistic model successfully describes the coupled ionic−electronic transport governing c-MOF device operation.

title: Atomic Layer Ordering of 2D van der Waals Ion Channels Enables Ultrathin and Highly Selective Membranes
abstract: Abstract Developing ultrathin, highly selective membranes that emulate biological ion channels is a primary goal of synthetic membrane technology. Although two-dimensional (2D) materials offer a promising platform for constructing subnanometer fluidic channels, simultaneously achieving high permeance and excellent selectivity in 2D ionic membranes remains a significant challenge. This bottleneck originates from the complexities involved in controlling the precise structural arrangement within nanosheet assemblies. In this work, we demonstrate that the atomic-layer ordering of 2D van der Waals (vdW) ion channels is a decisive factor in achieving ultrathin, highly selective membranes. By assembling 2D titania nanosheets with atomic layer-by-layer regularity, we fabricate atomic stacking membranes (ASMs) that achieve near-unity ion selectivity within an ultrathin (∼50 nm) framework. The structural regularity of these ASMs causes continuous overlap of the electrical double layer throughout the 2D ion channels, facilitating robust electrostatic regulation and maximizing selectivity. The result is further confirmed by transmission electron microscopy, grazing-incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering analysis, and molecular dynamics simulations. Leveraging the “Lego-like” modular assembly advantage of ASMs, we demonstrate multifunctional heterostructural iontronic devices and gate-controlled iontronic transistors featuring on/off ratios up to 104. Furthermore, the well-ordered 2D ion channels within these ASMs enable high-performance osmotic energy harvesting. This solution-processable atomic-layer van der Waals assembly strategy for ultrathin and highly selective ASMs establishes a versatile platform for uniformly regulating 2D angstrom-scale ion transport, paving the way for advanced biomimetic iontronics and efficient energy conversion.

title: Planar-Chiral Metal Clusters Direct Polarization-Responsive Supercrystals
abstract: Abstract Chiral metal clusters are promising atomically precise building blocks for hierarchical chiral materials, but their programmed assembly into structurally resolved supercrystals with traceable chirality transfer remains challenging. Here, we show that planar-chiral Cu5 clusters can serve as symmetry-defined modules for constructing polarization-responsive supercrystals. Through single-site capping control and symmetry-matched linker-directed coordination assembly, the Cu5 unit is organized into monomeric, dimeric, trimeric, and helical crystalline architectures, thereby enabling chirality to be traced from discrete clusters to higher-order supercrystalline structures. Single-crystal analyses reveal how the planar chirality of the cluster is encoded locally and propagated through distinct, orientationally ordered packing sequences. Quantitative Mueller matrix measurements show architecture-dependent circular and linear optical responses, including circular and linear retardance, which correlate with the crystallographic orientation and packing sequence of the Cu5 units, particularly Cu···Cu bonding. This work establishes planar-chiral metal clusters as versatile, stereochemically programmable synthons, providing a quantitative framework that links cluster-level chirality, arrangement orientation, and macroscopic polarization-dependent optical responses. The strategy offers a novel modular route to structurally defined chiral supercrystals, in which optical polarization responses can be traced to atomically resolved anisotropic sequences of chiral cluster assembly.

title: Colloidally Prepared Homogeneous Wide-Bandgap Perovskites for Efficient Tandem Solar Cells with Industrial Silicon
abstract: Abstract Wide-bandgap (WBG) perovskites, based on mixed halide-cation compositions, are widely employed as top cells in perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells to overcome the theoretical limitations of single-junction devices and exploit the full potential of crystalline silicon photovoltaics. However, uncontrolled nucleation rates and disordered crystallization kinetics in WBG perovskites pose a grave challenge to the preparation of phase-homogeneous perovskite films. Herein, we identify the undesirable precursor suspension as the main underlying reason for the compositional inhomogeneity and propose a colloidal engineering strategy to reconstruct the perovskite intermediate complex. According to classical colloidal theory and theoretical calculations, long-chain alkylphosphonic acid molecules are selected to precisely regulate colloidal structures and properties via their specific coordination strengths, leading to colloid-guided rapid nucleation and slow crystallization processes. Assisted by the uniform colloidal nucleation template, the prepared WBG perovskite films with compositional homogenization and reduced trap density enable tandem devices based on industrial silicon heterojunction cells to yield a champion power conversion efficiency of 34.01% (a certified reverse-scan PCE of 33.65%) for a 1 cm2 active area. The resultant encapsulated tandem device maintains 93% and 88% of its initial efficiency after 1211 h and 1000 h of one-sun operation at 25 and 65 °C, respectively, under their maximum power points.

title: Electronic Polarization of Covalent Organic Framework Membranes for Precise Antibiotic Purification
abstract: Abstract Precise molecular separation is essential for pharmaceutical production and purification, yet existing sieving systems struggle to distinguish structurally similar molecules due to their predominant reliance on size exclusion. Herein, we fabricate a covalent organic framework (COF) membrane featuring fluorine-induced polarized nanochannels for fast organic solvent nanofiltration. The incorporation of fluorine atoms redistributes electron density along the pore walls, creating a polarized electrostatic environment while lowering surface energy. This unique pore environment promotes the uptake and transport of polar solvents, while enhancing separation selectivity by retarding highly polar solutes through polarity-dependent solute-framework interactions. Furthermore, the low surface energy imparted by the robust C–F bonds also reduces irreversible foulant adhesion and facilitates permeance recovery after cleaning. The resultant COF membrane achieves a molecular weight cutoff down to 350 Da and stable operation for over 550 h. Notably, it differentiates structurally related fluoroquinolone antibiotics according to their molecular polarity and delivers a favorable separation factor of 8.9 for norfloxacin over its synthetic intermediate piperazine. This work demonstrates that engineering pore-wall polarity in COF membranes provides a viable route to chemically regulated molecular recognition beyond size-based separation.

title: Engineering Amino‐Induced p‐π Conjugation for Electronic Regulation of Li + Transport in PVDF‐Based Solid‐State Electrolytes
abstract: ABSTRACT Sluggish Li + transport in poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF)‐based solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) arises from restricted polymer segmental motion and persistent Li + ‐FSI − association, while conventional fillers provide limited regulation of the local electronic and coordination environments. Herein, amino‐functionalized UiO66‐NH 2 is introduced into a PVDF/lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (LiFSI) electrolyte to construct electronically active composite SPEs (U6NP). The electron‐donating ─NH 2 groups induce p‐π conjugation, redistribute the linker electron density, and strengthen ligand‐to‐metal charge transfer (LMCT)‐related electronic coupling between the organic linkers and Zr‐O clusters. This electronic reconstruction, together with amino‐associated modulation of local O‐centered coordination environments, reshapes the electrostatic landscape, weakens Li + ‐FSI − interactions, and facilitates Li + migration. U6NP delivers a room‐temperature ionic conductivity of 2.41 × 10 −3 S cm −1 , a Li + transference number of 0.56, and an oxidative stability of 4.42 V. More importantly, Li||U6NP||LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 (NCM811) cells with a cathode loading of 21.5 mg cm −2 retain 98.51% after 120 cycles at 0.05 C. The Li||U6NP||NCM811 pouch cell delivers 136.6 mAh g −1 initially and 120.9 mAh g −1 after 100 cycles. This work establishes ─NH 2 ‐induced p‐π conjugation‐enhanced LMCT as an effective strategy for electronically active MOF‐reinforced PVDF electrolytes toward high‐loading solid‐state lithium metal batteries.

title: Mitochondria‐Inspired COF Nanochannels for Reversible Directional Ion Transport for Osmotic Power Generation
abstract: ABSTRACT Directional ion transport in artificial nanochannels usually relies on fixed structural or chemical asymmetry, which restricts adaptive regulation. Inspired by proton transport in mitochondrial ATP synthase, we fabricate pH‐responsive PAN‐supported COF nanochannel membranes via liquid–liquid confined interfacial polymerization. Transmembrane pH polarization triggers asymmetric charge regulation and builds an internal electric field. The membranes show pH‐dependent ion transport, with conductance spanning 0.4–1005.5 µS and a forward/reverse power density ratio of 202. Under a 100‐fold NaCl gradient and pH 1/13 polarization, they deliver 20.2 W m − 2 . Experiments verify pH‐dependent COF charge regulation, while simulations indicate internal electric fields modulate ion migration together with diffusion. Salinity and pH gradients supply transport driving force; COF charge regulation dominates directional transport, and electrolyte properties, ion mobilities and electrochemical potentials tune current and output power. The observation of analogous directional transport across six chemically distinct membrane systems suggests the broader applicability of pH‐mediated transport regulation. These results provide insight into adaptive ion regulation and a strategy for energy conversion under combined salinity and pH gradients.

title: Self‐Confinement‑Tailored Energy Routing for Superior Thermal‐Adaptive Ln‐MOFs Scintillator
abstract: ABSTRACT Noncontact radiation monitoring in extreme environments is essential across scientific and industrial fields, driving the development of x‑ray scintillators. Conventional scintillators continue to suffer from inadequate exciton utilization, poor thermal stability, or limited processability. In this study, we propose a self‐confinement strategy to tailor energy routing for constructing superior thermal‐adaptive scintillators. Two lanthanide‐organic frameworks, ZJNU‐1006‐Ln and Ln‐BDC‐F, are rationally designed and synthesized. Compared with the free state of pure ligand or its quasi‐confinement state in Ln‐BDC‐F, ZJNU‐1006‐Ln exhibits a strong molecular self‐confinement state arising from compact ligand packing, thereby enhancing exciton utilization, suppressing nonradiative energy dissipation, and optimizing the energy routing. These features endow ZJNU‐1006‐Ln with superior radio‐luminescent performance, including high light yield (max ∼ 62,000 photons MeV ‒1 ), low detection limit (92.7 nGy air s ‒1 ), and great thermal‐stability (< 7% emission intensity attenuation from 77 to 590 K). ZJNU‐1006‐Ln membranes and fibers demonstrate great potential for in situ, real‐time x‐ray imaging and radiation monitoring. title: Spatial Electrostatic Complementarity in MOF Pores Enables Selective Recognition of Closely Related Fluoromethanes
abstract: ABSTRACT Trace purification of chemically similar gases is particularly challenging when molecular size and kinetics offer little contrast and conventional affinity descriptors provide conflicting guidance. Trifluoromethane (CHF 3 ) removal from monofluoromethane (CH 3 F) exemplifies this problem: CH 3 F has the greater dipole moment, and CHF 3 is more polarizable. Here, to our knowledge, we report the first adsorptive removal of trace CHF 3 from CH 3 F and demonstrate electrostatic complementary recognition (ECR) in interpenetrated anion‐pillared MOF pores. Localized, directional negative‐potential sites from TiF 6 2– pillars and surrounding electropositive pyridyl C─H domains complement the 1H/3F electrostatic pattern of CHF 3 while geometrically frustrating the inverse 3H/1F pattern of CH 3 F. All other benchmark adsorbents showed an overall preference for CH 3 F, whereas both TIFSIX frameworks achieved a reversal of adsorption preference toward CHF 3 under trace‐relevant conditions. TIFSIX‐Cu‐dpt, featuring a more focused and directional ECR environment, adsorbed 18.5 cm 3 /g of CHF 3 at 0.1 kPa. Neutron diffraction, adsorption thermodynamics, and molecular simulations support a spatially complementary multipoint binding mode. Fixed‐bed breakthrough of a binary feed containing 1000 ppm CHF 3 produced CH 3 F with >99.999% purity relative to CHF 3 at 320 L/kg. These results show how spatial electrostatic complementarity can translate subtle molecular differences beyond conventional scalar descriptors into selective adsorption.

title: Engineering Stable and Targeted NIR/SWIR Imaging Agents through Metal-Organic Framework Nanoconfinement
abstract: Near-infrared (NIR) and shortwave infrared (SWIR) fluorophores offer significant potential for biomedical imaging owing to their deep tissue penetration and low background autofluorescence. However, their widespread application remains limited by poor aqueous solubility, aggregation-induced fluorescence loss, and inadequate stability in physiological environments. Here, we present a general nanoconfinement strategy that converts hydrophobic molecular fluorophores into stable, bright, and engineerable imaging nanocomposites through encapsulation within the large-pore metal-organic framework ZIF-71. Using IR-780 as a model dye and extending the approach to the larger fluorophores IR-813 and IR-1048, we demonstrate that in situ encapsulation preserves a predominantly monomeric dye population within the ZIF-71 framework, effectively suppressing aggregation across diverse aqueous environments, including physiologically relevant and high-salinity conditions. Compared with free dyes and benchmark micellar formulations, the IR-780@ZIF composites exhibit markedly improved resistance to aggregation, enhanced solution and photostability, and substantially increased fluorescence quantum yields and imaging brightness in water and phosphate-buffered saline. The benefits of confinement become increasingly pronounced for larger and more hydrophobic fluorophores, turning essentially dark free dyes IR-813 and IR-1048 in aqueous media into bright composites. Importantly, the external surface of the ZIF particles can be modified orthogonally through post-synthetic functionalization without compromising the optical properties of the encapsulated fluorophore. Surface incorporation of biotin and cell-penetrating peptide ligands enables tailored cellular delivery of the fluorophores, demonstrating the modularity of the platform. Collectively, these results establish large-pore ZIFs as versatile hosts for molecular NIR/SWIR fluorophores and highlight MOF nanoconfinement as a powerful strategy for integrating high-performance photophysics with customizable biological functionality for advanced imaging applications.

title: Self-Assembly of Sub-10 nm Lamellar Domains with Controlled Orientation Using Fluorinated Junctions
abstract: Abstract We studied the thin-film self-assembly behavior of low-molecular-weight symmetric block copolymers (BCPs) of poly(solketal methacrylate) (PSM) and polystyrene (PS), with and without a poly(hexafluoroisopropyl acrylate) low-surface-energy (LSE) junction, PSM-b-F-b-PS and PSM-b-PS, respectively. An in situ hydrolysis of the PSM block to hydrophilic poly(glyceryl monomethacrylate) (PGM) markedly increased the segmental interaction parameter, χ. The high-χ, low-N copolymers self-assembled into horizontal or vertical lamellae with a center-to-center distance between adjacent lamellae (full pitch) of 9.4 nm. A free-energy analysis of the thin-film self-assembly on native Si predicted that the LSE junctions would induce an orientation of the lamellae for PGM-b-F-b-PS normal to the surface with only a few segments of the LSE junction. In comparison, an orientation of the lamellae parallel to the surface with an island-hole surface topography resulted from PGM-b-PS. We note that vertical lamellae were observed at the edges of islands and holes where the thickness transits from one thickness commensurate with the full pitch to another. Atomic force microscopy (AFM) and grazing-incidence small-angle X-ray scattering (GI-SAXS) results matched the free-energy predictions. With LSE junctions, uniform vertical orientation of the self-assembled lamellae was obtained, eliminating the need to modify the substrate or apply external fields to obtain this orientation, significantly simplifying preparation.

title: Self‐Assembly and Bimodal Chemical Activation of Dibromodibenzothiophene S ‐Oxide on Au(111)
abstract: ABSTRACT The rapidly growing on‐surface synthesis toolbox is currently developing toward reaction schemes of increasing complexity, namely by the use of polyfunctional and non‐planar precursors. We present an extensive experimental and theoretical investigation of the on‐surface self‐assembly and reactivity of dibromodibenzothiophene S ‐oxide on the Au(111) surface in ultrahigh vacuum in submonolayer regime. Several phases are observed after room‐temperature deposition depending on the coverage, with the dibenzothiophene backbone parallel to the surface and the oxygen pointing downward. Upon thermal activation, deoxygenation of the sulfoxide group and dissymmetric dehalogenation are sequentially initiated, leading to an unexpected organometallic intermediate phase with singly debrominated molecules. The deoxygenation reaction induces electronic structure modifications and chemical shifts in the sulfur as well as the carbon core levels. The final product after complete Ullmann coupling consists in dibenzothiophene nanoribbons. The importance of halogen bonding in the formation of “closed‐shell” clusters and in the stabilization of the singly debrominated domains is highlighted. Our results, based on scanning probe microscopy, x‐ray spectroscopy, and diffraction measurements, supported by theoretical modeling at the density functional theory level, provide insights into the intrinsic dependence of structure and reactivity in on‐surface synthesis.

title: Phosphorus-mediated reverse hydrogen spillover enables rate-matched nitrate-sulfate paired electrolysis for ammonium persulfate synthesis
abstract: Electrochemical conversion of nitrate-contaminated wastewater into value-added ammonium products offers a promising pathway, yet practical implementation is hindered by sluggish nitrate reduction kinetics and poor redox rate matching in paired electrolysis systems. Here we report a phosphorus-mediated reverse hydrogen spillover mechanism that enables kinetically synchronized nitrate reduction and sulfate oxidation for the direct electrosynthesis of ammonium persulfate ((NH4)2S2O8). In situ spectroscopic measurements and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations show that the PdP2@Cu3P heterointerface catalyst dynamically shuttles active hydrogen from hydrogen-generation sites to nitrate-activation sites, revealing rapid P-mediated hydrogenation at the interface, thereby decoupling hydrogen production from consumption and bypassing the multistep proton-coupled electron transfer pathway. The catalyst achieves a nitrate reduction rate of 8.94 × 10⁻7 mol cm⁻2 s⁻1, an ammonia Faradaic efficiency exceeding 92%, and sustained operation at 220 mA cm⁻2. In a membrane-electrode paired electrolyzer, the system produces (NH4)2S2O8 at a rate of 1.6 mmol h⁻1 cm⁻2, with 55% lower energy consumption and ~99.6% lower CO2 emissions than conventional routes. This work establishes a general strategy for nitrate–sulfate wastewater valorization and high-value oxidant production. Electrochemical conversion of nitrate-rich wastewater to valuable ammonium salts is promising. We report a phosphorus-mediated reverse hydrogen spillover mechanism that synchronizes nitrate-reduction and sulfate-oxidation kinetics, enabling direct electrosynthesis of ammonium persulfate.

title: Co‐Assembly and Metal‐Ion‐Driven LCST Engineering in Programmable Supramolecular Nanoarchitectonics for Climate‐Adaptive Energy‐Efficient Technologies
abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving energy‐efficient control of solar radiation requires intelligent materials capable of dynamically responding to environmental stimuli. Thermoresponsive systems exhibiting lower critical solution temperature (LCST) transitions offer an attractive strategy for passive and reversible modulation of light transmission. Herein, we report three xanthone‐based bolaamphiphiles with varying oxyethylene chain lengths that undergo thermoresponsive supramolecular self‐assembly in water. The resulting spherical nanoaggregates exhibit temperature‐dependent light scattering, enabling reversible switching between transparent and opaque states. XFO 2 and XFO 3 display distinct LCST transitions at 10°C ± 0.03°C and 33.14°C ± 0.03°C, respectively. Stoichiometric mixing of XFO 2 and XFO 3 enables programmable LCST regulation across 10°C–33°C through mixed/co‐assembled supramolecular states with minimal thermal hysteresis. XFO 3 further exhibits metal‐ion‐driven LCST modulation in the presence of Fe 3 + and Al 3 + . Leveraging these complementary tuning strategies, a 24 × 24 cm 2 prototype demonstrates rapid reversible optical switching between 30°C and 37°C and stable operation over 6000 cycles across 12 months. High solar (ΔT so l = 88.6%) and infrared (ΔT IR = 87.5%) transmittance modulation further demonstrates the potential of this supramolecular platform for climate‐adaptive, energy‐efficient smart‐window technologies.

title: Topological‐Insulator‐Based Ion‐Electron‐Coupled Nanochannels With a Photothermally Induced Thermoelectric Field for Enhanced Ionic Transport
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient ion transport is essential for high‐performance energy storage and conversion, yet strong ion–channel interactions in conventional highly polar nanochannels can increase migration barriers and impede rapid ion motion. Here, we report layered ion‐electron‐coupled Bi 2 Te 3 /Ti 3 C 2 T x nanochannels, in which ion transport is synergistically regulated by highly polar interfaces, highly conductive surface states, and a photothermally induced thermoelectric field. The polar MXene interfaces support selective ion transport, whereas the highly conductive surface states of Bi 2 Te 3 enhance interfacial electronic responsiveness, facilitating charge equilibration and mitigating local charge accumulation during ion migration. This interfacial coupling reduces the ion‐transport activation energy to 8.02 kJ mol −1 , 34.6% lower than that of pristine MXene nanochannels. As a functional demonstration of enhanced ion transport, the nanochannels deliver a 5.56‐fold increase in osmotic power density (18.9 W m −2 ) under a 50‐fold NaCl concentration gradient. Upon illumination, the photothermally induced temperature gradient activates the Seebeck response of Bi 2 Te 3 , providing an additional thermoelectric driving force for directional ion migration, as reflected by a further increase in power density to 25.5 W m −2 . This work provides a strategy for enhancing ion transport under nanoconfinement through interfacial‐electronic‐coupling‐mediated regulation and thermoelectric‐field‐assisted driving.

title: Ultra‐Strong, Leak‐Proof Bio‐Based Polyurethane Ionic Fibers for Sustainable Smart Wearables
abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence (AI)‐integrated digital flexible devices have been widely used in motion detection. However, the emphasis on sensitivity and response speed often overlooks environmental sustainability. Based on a green‐mechanical‐electrical synergistic design, a polar coordination and chemical confinement strategy is proposed to fabricate an ion‐conductive polyurethane fiber. Specifically, chemical confinement refers to the covalent incorporation of the polymerizable ionic‐liquid component into the polyurethane backbone through its hydroxyl‐functionalized imidazolium moiety. Polar coordination involves reversible Mg 2+ –carbonyl interactions that contribute to mechanical reinforcement and Mg 2+ retention. The resulting fiber exhibits a tensile strength of 52.75 MPa and an elongation at break of 1414%. Meanwhile, the in situ grafted ionic liquid provides an ionic conductivity of 0.209 mS cm −1 . After 120 h of vigorous stirring in water, the Mg concentration in the test medium reached 1.9 ppm, showing limited Mg release under the tested condition. Integrating this fiber into smart fabrics enables full‐body motion monitoring and accurate recognition of complex movements with 100% accuracy. This study establishes a closed‐loop paradigm from sustainable molecular design to AI‐driven decision‐making, offering new material design insights for next‐generation green, safe, and high‐performance smart wearable devices.

title: π‑Conjugated Helical Polymer for Circularly Polarized Photodetection and Secure Optoelectronic Encoding
abstract: ABSTRACT Helical polymers are promising materials for circularly polarized light (CPL) detection and hardware‐level information security owing to their tunable chiroptical properties, efficient charge transport, and intrinsic conformational randomness. However, designing helical polymers with high chiroptical activity, which can be effectively translated intohigh‐performance CPL detection remains challenging. Herein, we reported the helical polymer, ( SSSS )‐diPDI‐C8‐T‐T, in which point chirality was effectively transferred to π‐extended diperylene diimide (diPDI) backbone. Compared with non‐helical polymer ( SS )‐PDI‐C8‐T‐T, ( SSSS )‐diPDI‐C8‐T‐T exhibited chiroptical activity (the absorption dissymmetry factors, g abs = −1.4 × 10 −3 at 460 nm) in chloroform (10 −5 M), owing to the optimized electric–magnetic ( µ ‐ m ) transition dipole alignment. CPL detectors based on ( SSSS )‐diPDI‐C8‐T‐T annealed thin films exhibited higher average photocurrent dissymmetry factors ( g ph ) of 0.52 at 535 nm and −1.03 at 405 nm, the latter of which is the highest g ph reported for single‐component chiral polymer‐based CPL detection. The enhanced chirality‐induced spin selectivity (CISS) effect increased the spin polarization to 89.03%, contributing to the higher g ph for ( SSSS )‐diPDI‐C8‐T‐T annealed thin films. Leveraging the dual‐wavelength CPL response of ( SSSS )‐diPDI‐C8‐T‐T annealed thin films and spatial randomness, 5 × 8 CPL‐PUF array enabled optoelectronic fingerprinting, with inter‐ and intra‐Hamming distances of 49.278% and 1.655%, respectively. This work highlights helical polymers for CPL detection and chiral optoelectronic fingerprinting.

title: Antiaromaticity for Through-Space Molecular Thermoelectricity
abstract: Abstract Charge transport in molecular junctions has largely relied on aromatic frameworks, where intramolecular π-delocalization stabilizes the electronic structure but inherently limits intermolecular electronic coupling. Here we show that antiaromatic Ni(II) norcorrole assemblies outperform their aromatic counterparts in thermally driven charge transport. This superior performance arises from strong intermolecular coupling, facilitated by the externalized electronic stabilization of antiaromatic building blocks. Such strong intermolecular coupling enables unusually thick molecular stacks within molecular junctions and yields Seebeck coefficients of up to 600 μV K–1, far exceeding those of the aromatic analogue. Quantum transport calculations reveal that π–π stacking in the antiaromatic assemblies shifts the HOMO transmission resonance closer to the Fermi level while progressively narrowing it, accounting for the substantial enhancement of the Seebeck coefficient while maintaining efficient long-range charge transport with a low tunneling attenuation coefficient. These findings establish antiaromaticity as a design principle for thermoelectric energy conversion based on collective intermolecular coupling rather than isolated molecular orbitals.

title: Regulating Functionalized MXene Crystal-Field Splitting toward Efficient Bifunctional Oxygen Electrocatalysis of Lithium–Oxygen Batteries
abstract: Abstract MXenes offer fast conductive frameworks with abundant intrinsic active metal sites, making them promising cathode catalysts for lithium–oxygen batteries for addressing sluggish oxygen kinetics and severe cathode passivation. However, the predictive electronic descriptors for rationally regulating these intrinsic active sites remain elusive. Here, we demonstrate the implementation of crystal-field splitting engineering at Ti sites of Ti3C2-MXene to achieve bifunctional oxygen electrocatalysis. Through coordinated anionic and cationic modifications, we regulate the local coordination environment of Ti atoms, weakening crystal-field splitting and promoting electron delocalization within Ti3C2-MXene frameworks. X-ray absorption spectra reveal systematic shifts of Ti K-edge and contraction of the pre-edge splitting, consistent with weakened and distorted Ti ligand fields. This electronic rearrangement promotes an asymmetric Li2O2 adsorption configuration, thereby lowering the energy barriers for both ORR and OER. Consequently, the functionalized Cu–Ti3C2Br2 delivers a high discharge specific capacity of 11,662 mAh g–1 and reduces the initial charge overpotential by 50% compared with Ti3C2OF. This study indicates crystal-field splitting as a key descriptor governing oxygen electrocatalytic behavior in lithium–oxygen batteries.

title: Inorganic Ionic Polymerization toward Fracture-Resistant, Self-healable Functional Hydrogels
abstract: Abstract Fracture-resistant, self-healable functional hydrogels hold promise for soft robotics, wearable electronics, and intelligent devices. However, integrating these properties within a single structure remains challenging. Persistent load-bearing constraints hinder molecular rearrangement for repair, whereas excessive network dynamics can disrupt functional organization. Here, we uncover a reciprocal assembly mechanism based on bidirectional regulation between inorganic ionic oligomers and polymer chains. The acrylic acid/poly(acrylic acid) (PAA) environment suppresses calcium carbonate oligomer (CCO) aggregation, while CCO organizes PAA chains into birefringent acicular domains through multisite coordination and cooperative hydrogen bonding. These domains provide persistent load-bearing constraints and exchangeable interactions, enabling a fracture energy of 38.3 kJ m–2 and 87% tensile-strength recovery after 6 h of ambient healing. The same assembled network further exhibits 4.5% AM1.5G solar-weighted absorptivity and strong mid-infrared emission, remaining 5.1 °C cooler than neat PAA under simulated sunlight while retaining its cooling response for 21 days. This work establishes inorganic ionic oligomers as active reciprocal regulators of polymer organization, coupling dynamic network reconstruction with mechanical reinforcement and functional stability.

title: Nanoscale Reduced‐Porphyrinic Covalent Organic Frameworks with Modulated Absorption for Enhanced Photodynamic Therapy
abstract: ABSTRACT Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) offer an attractive platform for organizing nanophotosensitizers into ordered architectures for improving photodynamic therapy (PDT). However, the photochemical performance of conventional porphyrin‐based frameworks has largely been constrained by their limited optical absorption at longer wavelength and inefficient generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS). Herein, we report the first highly crystalline nanoscale COFs (nCOFs) incorporating reduced porphyrin units, chlorins, and bacteriochlorins, which exhibit markedly modulated light absorption photophysical activity and PDT efficacy. Chlorin‐ and bacteriochlorin‐based nCOFs (Ctp and Btp) were prepared via imine condensation of high‐purity monomers under oxygen‐ and light‐free conditions at room temperature, affording long‐range crystalline order while preserving the intrinsic optical properties of the reduced chromophores. Compared to porphyrin‐based COF, Btp exhibited pronounced bathochromic shifts with strong absorption in the 640–750 nm region and substantially enhanced ROS generation under 705 and 808 nm laser irradiation. In Ctp‐ and Btp‐mediated PDT, the photocytotoxicity toward MC38 cancer cells was significantly enhanced, with potent antitumor efficacy in a murine colorectal tumor model. This study establishes reduced porphyrin as a viable building block for highly crystalline COFs and highlights the potential of ordered chromophore engineering for expanding the photochemical functionality of nCOFs.

title: Covalent–Organic Frameworks for Food Waste Prevention: From Molecular Programming to Preservation, Sensing, and Packaging
abstract: ABSTRACT Food waste is a major global sustainability challenge, generating substantial economic losses and environmental burdens across production, distribution, and consumption. Covalent–organic frameworks (COFs), with their predictable composition and topology, tunable pore architectures, high crystallinity, and chemically addressable frameworks, provide a versatile platform for molecular‐level functional design. This review presents a function‐oriented perspective on COFs for food waste prevention. We first discuss how pore size, topology, surface chemistry, framework organization, and hierarchical transport pathways can be programmed to regulate molecular adsorption, confinement, release, and transport, thereby supporting preservation‐related functions. We then examine fluorescent COFs and COFs‐based nanozymes as complementary optical and catalytic signal‐transduction platforms for monitoring food quality deterioration and contamination markers, with emphasis on their construction strategies and underlying photophysical and catalytic mechanisms. These structure–function relationships are further discussed in the context of preservation and shelf‐life extension, food quality deterioration and contamination sensing and monitoring, and functional food packaging. Finally, key challenges associated with structural stability, mass transfer, functional integration, scalable synthesis, safety, and practical deployment are highlighted. By linking molecular programming with functional transduction and food‐system applications, this review provides design principles for advancing COFs toward more effective food waste prevention.

title: Mechanocatalytic Upcycling of Diverse Plastic Wastes via an Fe/SiO 2 Catalyst
abstract: ABSTRACT Upcycling plastic waste into high‐value chemicals is an attractive pathway for the sustainable development of human society. Here, we demonstrate the mechanocatalytic conversion of polyethylene, polypropylene, polystyrene, polyester, and their mixtures into valuable hydrogen (H 2 ) and methane (CH 4 ) gases on an iron (Fe) species‐dispersed silica (SiO 2 ) catalyst, achieving almost 100% conversion under mild conditions. During the mechanocatalytic process, Fe species from the milling balls were anchored to the surface of pristine SiO 2 nanoparticles, forming the Fe/SiO 2 catalyst. Simultaneously, the Fe and Si sites in the Fe/SiO 2 catalyst synergistically facilitate the C─H bond activation and C─C bond cleavage pathways, enabling a favorable dehydrogenation‒cracking‒hydrogenation process to produce commercially valuable H 2 and CH 4 . Notably, this catalytic system also exhibits exceptional versatility in processing mixed plastic wastes without requiring prior sorting, while maintaining robust cycling stability. No expensive components, toxic chemicals, or energy‐intensive thermal conditions are needed.

title: Green Electrochemical Synthesis of Antimicrobial Polyaldehyde Starch
abstract: Abstract Conventional aldehyde-based biocides raise environmental and safety concerns due to their toxicity and persistence in inhibiting microbiologically influenced corrosion (MIC) in numerous industrial applications. The present study introduces a rapid and sustainable method for synthesizing polyaldehyde starch through electrochemistry (PAS-EC) using soluble starch as feedstock in aqueous salt media with iridium–ruthenium electrodes. This approach has the potential to replace toxic oxidants with a safer alternative, while significantly reducing reaction time and enhancing overall process safety. By minimizing hazardous reagents and streamlining operational steps, it can also contribute to improved sustainability. Taken together, these features make electrochemical methods a promising pathway for application in industrial bioprocesses. Under optimized electrochemical conditions (15 mA cm–2, 15% NaCl, and 1 h), PAS-EC was obtained with 65% yield and a degree of oxidation exceeding 63%, surpassing the conventional periodate-oxidized dialdehyde starch (DAS-PO) with 50% yield and a 48% degree of oxidation. FTIR and NMR characterization confirmed the successful formation of aldehydic groups, while thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) revealed a decrease in thermal stability due to the modification in the structure of pure starch. Biocidal efficacy was assessed against six hydrocarbon-degrading bacterial strains that are extremely relevant to MIC and bioremediation under oil and gas field conditions. PAS-EC displayed promising and broad-spectrum antibacterial activity, with a maximum of 60% inhibition efficiency at 1000 ppm in comparison to glutaraldehyde. Overall, both PAS-EC and DAS-PO demonstrated promising biocidal performance, underscoring their potential as safer and more sustainable alternatives.

title: End-Group Functionalization Reshapes the Self-Assembly and Phase Behavior of Pluronic F68 in Water
abstract: Abstract Pluronic triblock copolymers based on poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO) and poly(propylene oxide) (PPO), with a PEO–PPO–PEO architecture, exhibit thermoresponsive self-assembly governed by the interplay among polymer hydration, micellization, and intermicellar organization. Here, we investigate how terminal bisurethane-methacrylate functionalization affects the aqueous self-assembly and phase behavior of Pluronic F68. The resulting derivative, termed F68-XL, was examined over broad concentration and temperature ranges using differential scanning calorimetry, rheology, small-angle X-ray scattering, and refractive-index measurements. End-group functionalization produces only modest changes in the micellization boundary but markedly alters the conditions under which higher-order micellar organization develops. Compared with pristine F68, F68-XL displays a displacement of the body-centered cubic ordered region toward higher temperatures and polymer concentrations, together with an unusual re-entrant liquid-like–solid-like–liquid-like rheological response at high concentrations. These findings indicate that terminal functionalization affects higher-order organization more strongly than primary micellization and highlight the sensitivity of intermicellar packing and phase stability to Pluronic chain-end chemistry. The photoreactive terminal groups additionally enable UV-induced covalent network formation, establishing the photo-cross-linking capability of F68-XL. Overall, this work identifies end-group functionalization as an effective strategy for modulating the thermoresponsive self-assembly and phase behavior of Pluronic F68 while introducing an additional route to covalent network formation.

title: Aromatic Substituent Engineering of Polypeptides for Tunable Self-Assembly and Multicolor Solution- and Aggregation-State Emissions
abstract: Abstract Luminescent polypeptides and corresponding nanoparticles with tunable morphology and luminescent colors have shown significant potential in optical encoding and bioimaging. Herein, a series of aromatic substituent-modified poly(l-glutamate) bearing dihydrodibenzothiophene, carbazole, and triphenylamine moieties are synthesized. Despite the same peptide backbone, these polypeptides exhibit green, yellow, and orange luminescence centered at 509, 604, and 681 nm in solution, respectively. Time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy reveals emission lifetimes of 113.7, 121.2, and 108.9 μs of the polypeptides, while the fluorescence quantum yields (Qy) are 4.0%, 9.3%, and 3.1%, respectively. Upon self-assembly, nanobowls and large compound micelles with emission wavelengths located at 501, 554, and 629 nm are obtained, which are significantly blue-shifted compared with that of the polypeptides. Benefiting from their tunable multicolor emission, these polypeptides are further demonstrated for luminescent anti-counterfeiting. This study provides a facile side-chain substitution strategy for constructing luminescent polypeptides with controlled emission in both solution and aggregation states.

title: Correlating the Solution Aggregation and Crystallite Orientation in n-Type Conjugated Polymers
abstract: Abstract The ability to control the crystallite orientation of conjugated polymers in the solid state is critical for enhancing their charge-transport properties. Compared with significant advances achieved for p-type conjugated polymers, control over the crystallite orientation of n-type conjugated polymers remains somewhat limited. Herein, two naphthalenediimide (NDI) polymers (NDI-2T and NDI-3T) were selected as model systems to investigate the formation and transformation of edge-on and face-on modes through solvent selection and post-processing thermal and solvent vapor annealing. In CHCl3, NDI-2T and NDI-3T exhibited weak and strong aggregation, resulting in respective face-on and edge-on modes in as-cast films. In chloronaphthalene (CN), their enhanced aggregation happened during the solution-to-film process, leading to more pronounced edge-on orientations. Furthermore, these two crystallite orientations of NDI-2T films were reversibly transformed through combined heating and solvent vapor annealing. These crystalline behaviors were closely related to their aggregation in solution, providing insights into the crystallization of n-type copolymers for optoelectronic applications.

title: A near-quantum-limited diamond maser amplifier operating at millikelvin temperatures
abstract: Abstract Current microwave quantum technologies require the amplification of weak signals with minimal added noise at millikelvin temperatures. To date, this stringent requirement has been met exclusively by superconducting technologies, such as Josephson or kinetic-inductance parametric amplifiers. A fundamentally distinct alternative approach could be offered by masers, the microwave counterpart of lasers, which were predicted as early as the 1950s to achieve quantum-limited noise performance under ideal conditions. However, their dependence on cryogenic operation historically limited further advancement. Here we demonstrate the first-ever non-superconducting, near-quantum-limited maser amplifier operating at millikelvin temperatures utilising nitrogen impurity spins (P1 centres) in diamond. Population inversion is achieved via microwave pumping, exploiting a four-spin cross-relaxation mechanism. We realise a maximum power gain exceeding 30 dB, an added noise of approximately 2.55 quanta above the standard quantum limit, and a maximum 1 dB output compression point of −63 dBm at 6.595 GHz. The ability to operate in strong static magnetic fields of arbitrary orientation may offer a complementary, non-superconducting route for applications such as semiconducting spin-qubit readout, magnetic-resonance spectroscopy, and dark-matter axion searches.

title: Atomic‐Level Modulation of Boron Sites via Cobalt Single Atoms on CO 2 ‐Derived Carbon for Efficient H 2 O 2 Electrosynthesis
abstract: Electrochemical two‐electron oxygen reduction (2e − ORR) is an attractive alternative route for the production of hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ). Boron (B)‐doped carbon materials have been widely investigated for selective H 2 O 2 electrosynthesis. However, the most stable and abundant B configuration in the carbon basal plane shows limited catalytic performance, requiring a strategy to tune it into highly active B sites. Herein, a cobalt (Co) single‐atom‐modulated B‐doped porous carbon (ZNCC‐0.015) is synthesized through a one‐pot CO 2 conversion process using NaBH 4 and ZIF‐67. The Co─N 4 configuration electronically modulates neighboring B sites by electron transfer from the less electronegative Co to B, thereby optimizing OOH* adsorption energy and enabling B to function as a more efficient active site. ZNCC‐0.015 exhibits highly active and selective (>80%) performance for H 2 O 2 production, achieving an onset potential of 0.780 V versus RHE and improved ORR kinetics. It maintains a Faradaic efficiency (FE) above 80% over a wide potential window in the H‐cell, with a maximum H 2 O 2 production rate of 3.98 mol g cat −1 h −1 under bulk electrolysis conditions. This work proposes that transition metals regulate the electronic structure of adjacent heteroatoms in carbon frameworks, thereby tuning them into active sites for efficient H 2 O 2 electrosynthesis.

title: Integrated Valorization of Rapeseed Meal Through Fractionation: Pyrolysis-Based Conversion and Functional Polysaccharides
abstract: In a context marked by increasing pressure on raw material resources, growing environmental concerns, and the need to valorize all fractions generated from agricultural processing, the use of plant-based by-products, which are consistently available and generated in large quantities, appears to be a promising approach for optimizing the valorization of biomass resources. Rapeseed meal is the main by-product of rapeseed oil extraction and has traditionally been used as a protein source for animal feed. However, rapeseed meal is a complex material containing not only proteins, but also fiber-associated components, polysaccharides, phenolic compounds, minerals, and antinutritional factors. This diversity of constituents limits the effectiveness of a single utilization pathway, but also offers opportunities for differentiated valorization strategies. The fractionation of rapeseed meal and the separate utilization of its different fractions therefore represent a practical approach to better match the various constituents of rapeseed meal with appropriate valorization pathways. Accordingly, this thesis focused on the utilization of rapeseed meal fractions by relating differences in their composition to the selection of appropriate subsequent valorization pathways. Tail-end dehulling was first applied to redistribute the major components of rapeseed meal and to generate fractions with different compositional characteristics. The fine fraction contained more protein, amino acids, total phenolics, glucosinolates, phytic acid, Zn, Mg, and P, whereas structural fiber and total sugars were enriched in the coarse fraction. In particular, 64.75%, 60.80%, and 61.01% of the recovered NDF, ADF, and ADL, respectively, were distributed to the coarse fraction. The coarse fraction was therefore selected for thermochemical conversion. Thermogravimetric analysis at 5, 10, 20, 30, and 40 °C/min showed multistage decomposition. Activation energies ranged from 108.88 to 147.40 kJ/mol using the KAS method and from 112.44 to 151.20 kJ/mol using the OFW method, while Coats–Redfern analysis identified A1/4 and A1/3 as the most appropriate models for the two main conversion regions. The coarse fraction was subsequently pyrolyzed at 600 °C, producing 26.78% biochar. Pyrolysis increased fixed carbon and higher heating value and reduced the atomic H/C and O/C ratios to 0.52 and 0.13, respectively. The biochar had a pH of 9.31, electrical conductivity of 1.05 dS/m, cation exchange capacity of 18.6 cmolc/kg, and BET specific surface area of 1.09 m²/g, with a predominantly mesoporous pore-size distribution and enrichment of major mineral elements. Rapeseed meal carbohydrates represent another important component group for further valorization. Alkaline extraction of rapeseed meal polysaccharides was II optimized using a Box–Behnken design, and meal husk polysaccharide (HMP) and meal kernel polysaccharide (KMP) were obtained from coarse and fine fraction, respectively. Both HMP and KMP were high-molecular-weight, low-polydispersity polysaccharides rich in arabinose and galactose and showed broadly similar molecular-weight distributions, FTIR spectra, and partially amorphous structures. Methylation and NMR analyses showed that both were arabinan-dominated composite polysaccharides containing RG-I, xylan, galactan, and glucan domains, with differences mainly in the relative proportions of structural units. Both HMP and KMP exhibited DPPH, ABTS, and hydroxyl radical scavenging activities and effectively inhibited browning in fresh-cut apples, with KMP showing relatively stronger DPPH, ABTS, and anti-browning performance. Overall, this thesis demonstrates that the compositional heterogeneity of rapeseed meal can be exploited through fractionation to support differentiated valorization. The results support the use of the fiber-enriched coarse fraction for pyrolysis and biochar production and demonstrate the structural and functional potential of rapeseed meal polysaccharides for food-related applications. From a practical perspective, the preliminary economic comparison showed that coarse-fraction pyrolysis could increase the overall value by approximately 14% compared with direct feed utilization of the whole meal, while efficient ethanol recovery is critical for improving the economic feasibility of polysaccharide production. These findings provide scientific and practical support for the targeted utilization and further valorization of rapeseed meal.

title: Buried Interfacial Transport Governs Oxide-Protected Electrocatalysis
abstract: Abstract Protective overlayers are widely used to stabilize metal catalysts under harsh electrochemical conditions. Unlike graphene coatings, oxide overlayers introduce a buried metal-oxide interface that fundamentally reshapes reaction pathways by separating proton delivery from product release. Although proton transport through oxides has been extensively investigated, the fate of reaction products at buried interfaces remains unresolved; for example, H2-molecule vs H-atom pathways remain under debate in oxide-protected hydrogen evolution. Here, we revisit this buried interface using a microelectrochemical cell with well-defined model structures. Systematic measurements across nine metal-oxide heterostructures, combined with density functional theory calculations, reveal that product transport is governed by two sequential kinetic barriers: hydrogen spillover across the metal-oxide junction and hydrogen permeation through the oxide lattice. These coupled barriers determine whether reaction products are released, accumulate at buried interfaces, or induce interfacial failure. This work not only identifies superior Pt-TiO2 and Pd-TiO2 but also clarifies which step is impeded in Au-TiO2, Pt-SiO2, Pt-HfO2, Pd-SiO2, Pd-HfO2, Au-SiO2, and Au-HfO2 heterostructures. Guided by these model studies, we implement a TiO2 protection strategy in a proton-exchange-membrane water electrolyzer with remarkable durability. These findings provide a framework for constructing a complete proton-to-product route for buried interfaces, potentially resolving long-standing ambiguities in oxide-protected electrocatalysis.
